**Ch 039 draft — preliminary scan**

The "Conservative Christian Anarchy" subplot is on the authorized removal list, yet the draft retains a condensed version of it (starting "Adams had played with anarchy…He had elaborated, half in jest, a doctrine of Conservative Christian Anarchy"). That material survived the drafter's compression choice, so seams *within* it are fair game.

Key passage to examine:

> "He had elaborated, half in jest, a doctrine of Conservative Christian Anarchy, drawn from Hegel and Schopenhauer rightly understood. By the necessity of their philosophical descent, **each member of the fraternity denounced the other** as unequal to his lofty task…"

In the source, "each member of the fraternity" refers to the two-person party of Adams and Bay Lodge. Bay Lodge has been removed as an authorized cut. In the draft, Bay Lodge has not been introduced anywhere before this sentence. The phrase "each member of the fraternity" implies a named, plural membership that the draft has never established—only Adams has been mentioned. The antecedent for "each member" / "the fraternity" is missing from the draft.

> "…the student asked the Senator whether he should allow three generations, or more, to swing the Russian people into the Western movement."

In the source, the Senator is Senator Cameron, who was introduced earlier and whose role was set up. Cameron is on the authorized minor-character removal list. However, in the draft, "the Senator" appears with a definite article and no prior introduction anywhere in the chapter draft. This is a dangling definite reference — but Cameron is on the authorized removal list, so this is an authorized-cut residue. **Not a finding.**

Back to the "fraternity" issue: Bay Lodge is on the authorized removal list. The draft chose to keep the Conservative Christian Anarchy doctrine passage (the authorized subplot removal says "The 'Conservative Christian Anarchy' joke party with Bay Lodge (Ch 039)" is removed, yet the draft retained the doctrine). Since the drafter *kept* this passage rather than removing it, the internal seam created by the absence of Bay Lodge — "each member of the fraternity denounced the other" — is a break in material the drafter chose to retain, not a residue of an authorized cut. The reader has no way to know who the second "member" is.

> "…the student asked the Senator whether he should allow three generations…"

As noted, the Senator is an authorized-cut character (Cameron). Residue of authorized cut. Not a finding.

**Ch 040 draft — preliminary scan**

> "This made of Hay the best schoolmaster since 1865."

In the source, this sentence is preceded by: "as education it gave new resources to an old scholar, for it made of Hay the best schoolmaster since 1865." The logical connector "This made of Hay…" in the draft refers to the preceding paragraph about the Secretary of State's role vis-à-vis Congress — that argument is present in the draft, so the connective "This" has a workable antecedent. Parseable.

The rest of Ch 040 appears structurally sound.
